reason: Melting the sample seems like the first step toward separating its solid grains, and it is the only available combination.
expectation: I expect the selected ice chip to melt, leaving the brown material suspended or settled in water; the filter may be useful afterward.

effect: Melting released the particles but erased their original positions, so the sample can reveal grain properties rather than their arrangement in the ice.
reaction: The loss of positional information is a useful reminder that preparation can change a sample.
reason: Filtering is the only offered combination and seems like a practical way to separate the solid grains from the meltwater.
expectation: I expect the cloth to retain at least some sediment for closer examination, though I don't know how much it will catch.

effect: The filter separated the solids from the water, leaving crowded material ready for examination under the microscope.
reaction: I’m curious whether the crowded particles will be distinguishable.
reason: The microscope is the only offered combination and directly addresses the new goal.
expectation: I expect to see details of the trapped particles, though their crowding may make them hard to distinguish.

effect: The microscope revealed a segmented, jointed body in the sediment. Its damaged condition and the loss of its original position make preserving unbroken ice important for further study.
reaction: I was surprised by the limbs and segments, and curious about what a whole specimen might reveal.

mostWorthwhile.text: Examining the membrane was the most worthwhile moment: it turned an unexplained brown band into a striking discovery and raised a concrete reason to preserve the remaining ice.

leastWorthwhile.text: Filtering felt like a predictable intermediate step, although it clearly served the investigation.

surprise.text: I did not expect the brown speck to have limbs and a segmented body. Melting also showed how sample preparation can destroy information about where particles were originally positioned.

arbitrary.text: None of the actions felt purposeless, though each step offered only one combination, leaving little room for a gameplay decision.

continue.text: Yes. I would want to find out how the ice is kept intact and what further examination reveals about the body.
